cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jesus says, “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.” Samaritan towns are off the route for this trip. He points the twelve to “…the lost sheep of Israel.” instead.

The answer is True, and it's right there in the list. Jesus says, “Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons.” That's four jobs, and none of them is small. I get nervous when I have to flip a whole tray without a crumb falling off.
The word is freely, friends. Jesus says, “Freely you have received; freely give.” The twelve got it as a gift, so they hand it out the same way. No price tag, no fine print.
The answer is a second tunic. Jesus says, “Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff…” So no spare tunic goes along. I'd miss my spare apron already.

The reason is that a worker deserves to be provided for. Jesus says, “for the worker is worthy of his provisions.” So the twelve are workers, and they'll be provided for along the way. Packing light is the easy part when someone else is handling supplies.
The word is stay. Jesus says to find out who is worthy and “…stay at his house until you move on.” One house, no hopping around. I like it, because I'd never leave a kitchen that smelled good.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it, but if it is not, let your peace return to you.” An unworthy home means the peace comes back to the twelve. Nothing gets lost along the way.

The answer is to shake the dust off their feet. If anyone won't welcome the twelve or heed their words, Jesus says, “…shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.” It's a clear sign as they walk away. Then they keep moving down the road.

The two cities are Sodom and Gomorrah. Jesus says, “…it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.” This is a serious line, so I'll say it plainly. He is talking about a town that won't welcome the twelve.

Jesus is asking the twelve to be sharp and pure at the same time. He says, “…be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.” Shrewd is the sharp part and innocent is the pure part, and He asks for both together. Not one or the other, both.
The word is synagogues, friends. Jesus says, “…they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.” He doesn't sugarcoat it. He says it straight.

The twelve will be there as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles. Jesus says, “On My account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.” Witnesses are people who speak about what they know. So being brought before governors and kings puts them there as people who speak about Him.

The promise is that they will be given what to say. Jesus says, “…do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.” So what to say gets handed to them in that hour. I'd still bring a cookie, but that's just me.

The word is Spirit. Jesus says, “For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” So when the twelve stand up to talk, they aren't doing it on their own. That takes a lot of pressure off the moment.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “You will be hated by everyone because of My name…” This one is heavy, and He says it plainly. The reason in the verse is His name.

The one who perseveres to the end is the one who will be saved. Jesus says, “…the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” Persevering means sticking with it all the way. It comes right after He says, “You will be hated by everyone because of My name…”
The answer is False, friends. Jesus says, “When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next.” He doesn't tell them to stand their ground there. They keep moving down the road.

The word is teacher. Jesus says, “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.” A disciple follows a teacher, and the twelve are His disciples. The line tells them where they stand next to Him.

The answer is that they will get it even more, friends. Jesus says, “If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!” Beelzebul is the name used for the ruler of the demons (Matthew 12:24). So if the head of the house got that name, the household can expect it too. Right before that, Jesus says, “It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and a servant like his master.” (Matthew 10:25)
